tender.title: CCS028 Therapeutic Assessment to Support Education and Health Care Plan Delivery
tender.description:
Derbyshire County Council, Derby City Council, Nottinghamshire County Council and Nottingham City Council (D2N2) form a regional cluster in which we aim to collaborate to deliver better outcomes for children.\\r\r
\\r\r
Within this cluster, it has become evident that there is a need for further support from external providers to ensure effective, timely and valuable delivery of assessments to support Education and Health Care Plan (EHCP) delivery for our Children, who require this support.\\r\r
\\r\r
To facilitate more cohesive and efficient delivery of therapeutic assessments which support EHCP delivery and to ensure better outcomes for children whose educational needs are the responsibility of the D2N2 Councils are publishing an opportunity for providers to join a framework.\\r\r
\\r\r
The services to be provided through this framework have been split into 4 lots:\\r\r
\\r\r
a) Lot 1: Educational Psychology\\r\r
b) Lot 2: Speech and Language Therapy\\r\r
c) Lot 3: Occupational Therapy and Sensory Therapy\\r\r
d) Lot 4: Physiotherapy\\r\r
\\r\r
Providers can tender for one or multiple lots, assessment and/or delivery, and do not need to deliver their services to all areas covered by the D2N2 Framework.\\r\r
\\r\r
The framework will be procured under the "Light Touch Regime" for Social and Other Specific Services, and the Councils anticipate that framework will be reopened periodically to new applicants.

tender.title: PS26212 - Energy Sector Threat Sharing and Analysis Centre
tender.description:
***** THIS IS AN AWARD NOTICE, NOT A CALL FOR COMPETITION *****

This procurement is being concluded following a mini competition under the GCA RM3764.3 - Cyber Security Services 3 DPS, DPS FILTER CATEGORY: NCSC Assured Services

Brief overview of the requirements being awarded

The Department of Energy Security & Net Zero (DESNZ) is responsible for ensuring that the UK has a resilient energy sector. With the increasing use of cyber as an offensive attack methodology, and an increasing pool of adversaries prepared to employ it, action is required to support the energy sector and protect critical infrastructure. 

DESNZ, in consultation with experts at the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), NESO and industry have identified an opportunity to strengthen threat analysis and sharing capabilities and collaboration with support from government in the GB energy sector.
  
DESNZ's engagement with the GB energy sector has revealed that many organisations face  significant challenges in understanding cyber threat and barriers to sharing information.

tender.title: DCI Online Forms Platform Services
tender.description:
The Department for Education (DfE) is re-procuring an Online Forms Platform that enables the development and management of digital forms supporting a wide range of business processes and user services across DfE and ESFA. The platform currently supports over 200 online forms, with approximately 100 forms published via GOV.UK, including several business-critical services.

The new solution must provide a secure, scalable low-code/no-code platform capable of rapid form development and deployment, publication through GOV.UK, workflow creation, and integration with internal and third-party systems. Key capabilities include secure evidence submission, save-and-return functionality, data validation and lookups (e.g. GIAS and Companies House), pre-population of data, reporting, CRM and Microsoft 365 integration, self-service support, and the migration of existing live forms with minimal disruption to users and departmental operations.

tender.title: Designing and Testing Behaviourally-informed Interventions
tender.description:
Designing and Testing Behaviourally-informed Interventions (Understanding and Addressing Vaccine Uptake and Hesitancy Across Livestock Disease Programmes)

The overall aim of this project is to develop an evidence-based understanding of the behavioural and social factors that influence vaccine uptake and hesitancy across a range of animal disease contexts, and to identify opportunities to improve the effectiveness of vaccination as a disease prevention, control and preparedness measure. The project will generate evidence to support the design and implementation of future vaccination policies and programmes, ensuring that behavioural considerations are integrated alongside epidemiological, economic and operational evidence.
Specifically, the project seeks to:
• Improve understanding of the factors influencing livestock keeper, veterinary and wider stakeholder decisions relating to vaccination.
• Identify common and disease-specific drivers, barriers and motivations affecting vaccine uptake, hesitancy and participation in vaccination programmes.
• Explore if and how behavioural influences vary across disease contexts, stakeholder groups, sectors and policy settings.
• Understand the role of trusted advisers, social networks, markets, supply chains, industry bodies and institutions in shaping vaccination decisions.
• Assess behavioural challenges associated with routine preventive vaccination, disease eradication programmes, and emergency vaccination deployed during disease outbreaks.
• Identify and test specific behavioural interventions, communications approaches and policy mechanisms that could increase vaccine uptake, support programme implementation and improve disease-control outcomes.
• Develop a transferable evidence base that can inform future vaccination policies across a range of animal health and welfare contexts.
